name: The Fairmont San Francisco
insider_take: This iconic Nob Hill landmark has been the crown jewel of San Francisco hospitality since 1907, rising from the ashes of the great earthquake to become a testament to the city's resilience and grandeur.
whats_special: The Fairmont sits atop prestigious Nob Hill, sharing the summit with Grace Cathedral and offering sweeping views of the San Francisco Bay. The hotel's stunning lobby features 22-foot coffered ceilings and marble columns, while the famous Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar houses a floating band and indoor rainstorms every 30 minutes. This is where the United Nations Charter was drafted in 1945, making it a site of global historical significance.
pro_tip: Book a room on the Bay View side for stunning sunrise views over Alcatraz and the Golden Gate Bridge. The hotel's cable car stop right outside means you can explore Fisherman's Wharf and Union Square without dealing with San Francisco's notorious parking situation.
dont_miss: Experience the legendary Tonga Room for tropical cocktails in a Polynesian paradise complete with thunderstorms, explore the nearby Cable Car Museum just blocks away, and take the short walk to Grace Cathedral to see the stunning indoor and outdoor labyrinths. The hotel's rooftop garden offers a secret escape with panoramic city views rarely seen by tourists.
pros: Iconic Nob Hill location with panoramic city views
Historic luxury hotel with timeless elegance and grandeur
Exceptional concierge and personalized guest services
Prime access to cable cars and major San Francisco attractions
cons: Historic building with some rooms showing age
